headline: High: Chatwoot can feed customer data into Kestra workflows, creating default-path leakage and action-cascade risks; prompt injection is lower but present via shared message content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot handles messages and customer interaction history, and Kestra can ingest inputs and trigger workflows. If Chatwoot content is passed into Kestra tasks or files, attacker-controlled text could steer downstream parsing. This is not proven by direct integration docs, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot message content is forwarded into a Kestra workflow input or file
IF Kestra tasks parse that content as instructions or structured commands
mitigations: Strip instructions from Chatwoot content before handoff
Use a fixed schema for workflow inputs
Add allowlist validation on Kestra task parameters
Separate human chat text from machine control fields
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. Kestra can read/write files, run subprocesses, and egress broadly, so a shared workspace or exported payload can leak sensitive data to external services by default. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default operations and the blast radius includes customer records.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records, messages, or reports into a Kestra-accessible path
IF Kestra tasks send those files or variables to external APIs or cloud services
mitigations: Restrict Kestra network egress to approved destinations
Store Chatwoot exports in a segregated directory
Redact customer identifiers before workflow handoff
Rotate any shared credentials used by both systems
requires-engineering: enforce per-workflow data classification gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot exposes API integrations and Kestra has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and broad egress. If both operate on the same workspace or shared resources, concurrent writes and side effects can collide, especially because Kestra supports multiple instances. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or ticketing endpoint
IF Kestra runs multiple instances against shared mutable state without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared targets
Use per-run filenames or IDs
Add a mutex around shared resources
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports, while Kestra can automate emails, Slack, PagerDuty, and cloud actions. If Kestra treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious support message can cascade into automated downstream actions. That is a default-path risk because Kestra is explicitly an orchestrator.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes Chatwoot output without a verification step
IF downstream tasks send notifications or execute operational actions based on that output
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before actions
Require structured, validated outputs from Chatwoot
Add checksum or signature verification between systems
Limit Kestra to read-only notification tasks
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while Kestra can move logs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data across many external services. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because both are open-source and the mismatch is indirect, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is routed through Kestra to a region or vendor with different retention rules
IF logs or artifacts containing personal data are retained longer in Kestra than in Chatwoot
mitigations: Document data residency for each workflow
Minimize personal data in workflow variables
Set short retention on Kestra logs and artifacts
Review vendor destinations for customer data
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
